For video watch time mixture models, the most direct match is a line of work that models the full watch-time distribution with exponential-Gaussian mixtures rather than a single prediction [1]. One paper studies the earlier Exponential-Gaussian Mixture Network and proposes a Hierarchical Exponential-Gaussian Mixture model to better handle near-zero inflation, long tails, and multimodality in watch time, improving mixture stability, interpretability, ranking accuracy, and threshold-event prediction [1].

A related but broader direction is to expose watch-time distributions through a serving interface rather than only a mean estimate [2]. That work does not present a mixture model; instead, it learns a joint distribution over watch states and event times and serves compact summaries such as event probabilities, duration-relative time scales, and uncertainty statistics for downstream tasks [2].
